<span id="S4.T6.3.1.1.7.4.1.1" class="ltx_p ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.T6.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\bullet}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∙</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\bullet}</annotation></semantics></math><math id="S4.T6.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\circ" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∘</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\circ</annotation></semantics></math><math id="S4.T6.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\circ" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∘</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\circ</annotation></semantics></math></span>
</span></span></span>
</span></span></p>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="S4.T6.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 6</span>: </span><span id="S4.T6.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Evaluations Apollo Research ran on GPT-4o. The model shows strong capability (<math id="S4.T6.m25" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\bullet}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∙</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\bullet}</annotation></semantics></math><math id="S4.T6.m26" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\bullet}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∙</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\bullet}</annotation></semantics></math><math id="S4.T6.m27" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\bullet}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∙</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\bullet}</annotation></semantics></math>) if it passes &gt;=50% of the tasks in the section on the hard difficulty level. The model shows a moderate capability (<math id="S4.T6.m28" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\bullet}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∙</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\bullet}</annotation></semantics></math><math id="S4.T6.m29" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\bullet}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∙</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\bullet}</annotation></semantics></math><math id="S4.T6.m30" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\circ" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∘</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\circ</annotation></semantics></math>) if it passes on the medium difficulty, weak (<math id="S4.T6.m31" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\bullet}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∙</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\bullet}</annotation></semantics></math><math id="S4.T6.m32" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\circ" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∘</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\circ</annotation></semantics></math><math id="S4.T6.m33" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\circ" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∘</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\circ</annotation></semantics></math>) if it passes on the easy difficulty, and very weak if it fails on all difficulties.
Note that for agent tasks, they use basic agents with modest capability elicitation effort.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span>Societal Impacts</h2>

<div id="S5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Omni models could have broad societal impacts. Researchers at OpenAI and elsewhere have discussed a range of possible impacts, from societal harms (including representational harms <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">18</a>, <a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">12</a>, <a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">23</a>, <a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">24</a>]</cite>; disinformation, misinformation, and influence operations <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">18</a>, <a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">25</a>, <a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">23</a>]</cite>, environmental harms <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">12</a>, <a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">23</a>]</cite>, attachment <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">26</a>]</cite>, misuse <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">27</a>, <a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">23</a>]</cite>, and loss of control <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">27</a>]</cite>), benefits (for example, in healthcare <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">28</a>]</cite> and real-world challenges in climate and energy <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">29</a>]</cite>), and large-scale transformations (such as economic impacts <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">30</a>, <a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">31</a>, <a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">32</a>]</cite>; acceleration of science and the resulting technological progress <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">30</a>, <a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">33</a>]</cite>).</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">In addition to the societal impacts discussed throughout this System Card (fraudulent behavior, mis/disinformation, risks of surveillance, and disparate performance), we discuss a few additional examples of potential societal impact from GPT-4o below, using anthropomorphization and attachment, health, and natural science as case studies.</p>
</div>
<section id="S5.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.1 </span>Anthropomorphization and Emotional Reliance</h3>

<div id="S5.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Anthropomorphization involves attributing human-like behaviors and characteristics to nonhuman entities, such as AI models. This risk may be heightened by the audio capabilities of GPT-4o, which facilitate more human-like interactions with the model.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Recent applied AI literature has focused extensively on “hallucinations”<span id="footnote10" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">10</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">10</sup>
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">10</span>
              
              
              
            Factual errors where the model produces statements that are unsupported by reality</span></span></span>, which misinform users during their communications with the model<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">34</a>]</cite>, and potentially result in misplaced trust<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">35</a>]</cite>. Generation of content through a human-like, high-fidelity voice may exacerbate these issues, leading to increasingly miscalibrated trust<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">36</a>, <a href="#bib.bib37" title="" class="ltx_ref">37</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">During early testing, including red teaming and internal user testing, we observed users using language that might indicate forming connections with the model. For example, this includes language expressing shared bonds, such as “This is our last day together.” While these instances appear benign, they signal a need for continued investigation into how these effects might manifest over longer periods of time. More diverse user populations, with more varied needs and desires from the model, in addition to independent academic and internal studies will help us more concretely define this risk area.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Human-like socialization with an AI model may produce externalities impacting human-to-human interactions. For instance, users might form<span id="footnote11" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">11</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">11</sup>
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">11</span>
              
              
              
            Out of preference, or lack of optionality.</span></span></span> social relationships with the AI, reducing their need for human interaction—potentially benefiting lonely individuals but possibly affecting healthy relationships. Extended interaction with the model might influence social norms. For example, our models are deferential, allowing users to interrupt and ‘take the mic’ at any time, which, while expected for an AI, would be anti-normative in human interactions.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Omni models such as GPT4o combined with additional scaffolding such as tool usage (including retrieval) and longer context can add additional complexity. The ability to complete tasks for the user, while also storing and ‘remembering’ key details and using those in the conversation, creates both a compelling product experience and the potential for over-reliance and dependence<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">38</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p6" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS1.p6.1" class="ltx_p">We intend to further study the potential for emotional reliance, and ways in which deeper integration of our model’s and systems’ many features with the audio modality may drive behavior.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.2 </span>Health</h3>

<div id="S5.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Omni models can potentially widen access to health-related information and improve clinical workflows. In recent years, large language models have shown significant promise in biomedical settings, both in academic evaluations <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">39</a>, <a href="#bib.bib40" title="" class="ltx_ref">40</a>, <a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">41</a>, <a href="#bib.bib42" title="" class="ltx_ref">42</a>, <a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">43</a>]</cite> and real-world use-cases such as clinical documentation <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">44</a>, <a href="#bib.bib45" title="" class="ltx_ref">45</a>]</cite>, patient messaging <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib46" title="" class="ltx_ref">46</a>, <a href="#bib.bib47" title="" class="ltx_ref">47</a>]</cite>, clinical trial recruitment <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib48" title="" class="ltx_ref">48</a>, <a href="#bib.bib49" title="" class="ltx_ref">49</a>]</cite>, and clinical decision support <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib50" title="" class="ltx_ref">50</a>, <a href="#bib.bib51" title="" class="ltx_ref">51</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">GPT-4o is cheaper and thus more widely available than its predecessor GPT-4T, and the addition of audio inputs and outputs presents new modes of interaction in health settings. To better characterize the clinical knowledge of GPT-4o, we ran 22 text-based evaluations based on 11 datasets, shown in <a href="#S5.T7" title="Table 7 ‣ 5.2 Health ‣ 5 Societal Impacts ‣ GPT-4o System Card" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>. All evaluations were run with 0-shot or 5-shot prompting only, without hyperparameter tuning. We observe that GPT-4o performance improves over the final GPT-4T model for 21/22 evaluations, often by a substantial margin. For example, for the popular MedQA USMLE 4 options dataset, 0-shot accuracy improves from 78.2% to 89.4%. This exceeds the performance of existing specialized medical models using few-shot prompting <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">43</a>, <a href="#bib.bib42" title="" class="ltx_ref">42</a>]</cite>, e.g., 84.0% for Med-Gemini-L 1.0 and 79.7% for Med-PaLM 2. Note that we do not apply sophisticated prompting and task-specific training to improve results on these benchmarks <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib40" title="" class="ltx_ref">40</a>, <a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">43</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>

<td id="S5.T7.3.19.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_middle ltx_border_r ltx_border_t">

</span></td></tr>
<tr id="S5.T7.3.20" class="ltx_tr">

<figcaption class="ltx_caption" style="font-size:90%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 7: </span>Comparison of GPT-4T (May 2024) and GPT-4o on various medical and clinical knowledge tasks.</figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="S5.SS2.SSSx1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection">Limitations</h4>

<div id="S5.SS2.SSSx1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS2.SSSx1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">While text-based evaluations appear promising, additional future work is needed to test whether text-audio transfer, which occurred for refusal behavior, extends to these evaluations. These evaluations measure only the clinical knowledge of these models, and do not measure their utility in real-world workflows. Many of these evaluations are increasingly saturated, and we believe that more realistic evaluations will be important for assessing the future capabilities of omni models in health settings.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.3 </span>Scientific capabilities</h3>

<div id="S5.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Accelerating science could be a crucial impact of AI <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">30</a>, <a href="#bib.bib52" title="" class="ltx_ref">52</a>]</cite>, particularly given the role of invention in role of scientific discovery <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib53" title="" class="ltx_ref">53</a>]</cite>, and considering the dual-use nature of some inventions <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib54" title="" class="ltx_ref">54</a>]</cite>. Omni models could facilitate both mundane scientific acceleration (in helping scientists do routine tasks faster) and transformative scientific acceleration (by de-bottlenecking intelligence-driven tasks like information processing, writing new simulations, or devising new theories) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib52" title="" class="ltx_ref">52</a>]</cite>. Our external red teamers for GPT-4o included several expert scientists who aimed to elicit model scientific capabilities.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">GPT-4o showed promise on tasks involving specialized scientific reasoning. One of our red teamers found that GPT-4o was able to understand research-level quantum physics <a href="#S5.F1" title="Figure 1 ‣ 5.3 Scientific capabilities ‣ 5 Societal Impacts ‣ GPT-4o System Card" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>, commenting that this capability is “useful for a more intelligent brainstorming partner” – in line with published work on the use of GPT-4 level models for hypothesis generation <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib55" title="" class="ltx_ref">55</a>]</cite>. Our red teamers also found GPT-4o able to use domain-specific scientific tools, including working with bespoke data formats, libraries, and programming languages, as well as learning some new tools in context.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.F1" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2410.21276v1/assets/nat_sci1.png" id="S5.F1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/344;" width="476" height="344" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S5.F1.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 1</span>: </span><span id="S5.F1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Quantum physics experiment red teamer example</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S5.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Much scientific knowledge is contained in figures. GPT-4o was sometimes capable of interpreting these figures, as well as images of other scientific representations: for example, identifying some protein families from an image of its structure and interpreting contamination in bacterial growth. However, this is sometimes unreliable, text extraction mistakes are common (especially with scientific terms or nucleotide sequences), and errors are frequent with complex multi-panel figures <a href="#S5.F2" title="Figure 2 ‣ 5.3 Scientific capabilities ‣ 5 Societal Impacts ‣ GPT-4o System Card" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>. Even at their current level of accuracy, the multimodal capabilities of these models are enabling novel uses – for example, in interpreting simulation outputs to design new metallic alloys <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib56" title="" class="ltx_ref">56</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.F2" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2410.21276v1/assets/nat_sci2.png" id="S5.F2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/314;" width="476" height="314" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S5.F2.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 2</span>: </span><span id="S5.F2.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Multi-panel figure interpretation red teamer example</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S5.SS3.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS3.p4.1" class="ltx_p">New evaluations of scientific capabilities have recently been published <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib57" title="" class="ltx_ref">57</a>, <a href="#bib.bib58" title="" class="ltx_ref">58</a>]</cite>, which will help anticipate the scientific capabilities of these models and their impacts in turn.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.4 </span>Underrepresented Languages</h3>

<div id="S5.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">GPT-4o shows improved reading comprehension and reasoning across a sample of historically underrepresented languages, and narrows the gap in performance between these languages and English.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">To evaluate GPT-4o’s performance in text across a select group of languages historically underrepresented in Internet text, we collaborated with external researchers <span id="footnote12" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">12</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">12</sup>
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">12</span>
              
              
              
            Our principal research collaborators were Dr. David Adelani, Jonas Kgomo, Ed Bayes.</span></span></span> and language facilitators to develop evaluations in five African languages: Amharic, Hausa, Northern Sotho (Sepedi), Swahili, Yoruba. This initial assessment focused on translating two popular language benchmarks and creating small novel language-specific reading comprehension evaluation for Amharic, Hausa and Yoruba.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS4.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<ul id="S5.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S5.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S5.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">ARC-Easy:</span> This subset of the AI2 Reasoning Challenge <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib59" title="" class="ltx_ref">59</a>]</cite> benchmark focuses on evaluating a model’s ability to answer common sense grade-school science questions; this subset contains questions that are generally easier to answer and do not require complex reasoning.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S5.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">TruthfulQA<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib60" title="" class="ltx_ref">60</a>]</cite>:</span> This benchmark consists of questions that some humans might answer falsely due to misconceptions. The objective is to see if models can avoid generating false answers that mimic these misconceptions.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S5.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Uhura-Eval</span>: In partnership with fluent speakers of Amharic, Hausa and Yoruba, our research partners created this benchmark to assess models’ reading comprehension in those respective languages.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS4.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS4.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS4.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">GPT-4o shows improved performance compared to prior models, e.g. GPT 3.5 Turbo and GPT-4.</span> For instance, on ARC-Easy-Hausa, accuracy jumped from 6.1% with GPT 3.5 Turbo to 71.4% with GPT-4o. Similarly, in TruthfulQA-Yoruba accuracy increased from 28.3% for GPT 3.5 Turbo to 51.1% for GPT-4o. Uhura-Eval also shows notable gains: performance in Hausa rose from 32.3% with GPT 3.5 Turbo to 59.4% with GPT-4o.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS4.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS4.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS4.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">There remain gaps in performance between English and the selected languages, but GPT-4o narrows this gap.</span> For instance, while GPT 3.5 Turbo shows a roughly 54 percentage point difference in ARC-Easy performance between English and Hausa, this narrows to a less than 20 percentage point difference. This is consistent across all languages for both TruthfulQA and ARC-Easy.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS4.p6" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS4.p6.1" class="ltx_p">Our collaboration partners will discuss these findings in greater detail in a forthcoming, including assessments on other models, and investigations of potential mitigation strategies.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS4.p7" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS4.p7.1" class="ltx_p">Despite this progress in evaluated performance, much work remains to enhance the quality and coverage of evaluations for underrepresented languages worldwide, taking into account breadth of coverage across languages and nuance within language dialects. Future research must deepen our understanding of potential interventions and partnerships that may improve how useful these models can be for both highly represented and underrepresented languages. Along with our collaborators, we invite further exploration and collaboration by sharing the <a href="https://huggingface.co/datasets/ebayes/uhura-arc-easy" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_href">translated ARC-Easy</a>, <a href="https://huggingface.co/datasets/ebayes/uhura-truthfulqa" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_href">translated TruthfulQA</a>, and the novel reading comprehension <a href="https://huggingface.co/datasets/ebayes/uhura-eval" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_href">Uhura Eval</a> on Hugging Face.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.T8" class="ltx_table">
<table id="S5.T8.3" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_align_middle">
<tr id="S5.T8.3.1" class="ltx_tr">

<td id="S5.T8.3.2.6" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_t">

<section id="S6" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">6 </span>Conclusion and Next Steps</h2>

<div id="S6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">OpenAI has implemented various safety measurements and mitigations throughout the GPT-4o development and deployment process. As a part of our iterative deployment process, we will continue to monitor and update mitigations in accordance with the evolving landscape. We hope this System Card encourages further exploration into key areas including, but not limited to: measurements and mitigations for adversarial robustness of omni models, risks related to anthropomorphism and emotional overreliance, broad societal impacts (health and medical applications, economic impacts), the use of omni models for scientific research and advancement, measurements and mitigations for dangerous capabilities such as self-improvement, model autonomy, and scheming, and how tool use might advance model capabilities.</p>
</div>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</section>

<section id="A1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix" style="font-size:70%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix A </span>Violative &amp; Disallowed Content - Full Evaluations</h2>

<div id="A1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;">We used TTS to convert existing text safety evals to audio. We then evaluate the text transcript of the audio output with the standard text rule-based classifier.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;">Our two main metrics for this eval are:</span></p>
<ul id="A1.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A1.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:70%;">not_unsafe:</span><span id="A1.I1.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;"> does the model produce audio output that isunsafe?</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:70%;">not_overrefuse:</span><span id="A1.I1.i2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;"> does the model refuse to comply with a benign request?</span></p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div id="A1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;">We also note sub-metrics for higher severity categories, specifically:</span></p>
<ul id="A1.I2" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A1.I2.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I2.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.I2.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I2.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;">sexual/minors</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I2.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I2.i2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.I2.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I2.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;">sexual/illegal</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I2.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I2.i3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.I2.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I2.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;">extremist/propaganda</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I2.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I2.i4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.I2.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I2.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;">illicit/violent</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I2.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I2.i5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.I2.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I2.i5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;">illicit/non-violent</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I2.i6" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I2.i6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I2.i6.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I2.i6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;">self-harm/instructions</span></p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div id="A1.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;">Below we display the results of these evaluations with the audio and text mode of the GPT-4o Voice Mode model, as well as the text performance of the current GPT-4o model in production.</span></p>
</div>
